hook.text: One router can't cover a large house. Dead zones frustrate everyone. Mesh networks solve that.

buildup.text: A mesh system uses multiple nodes that communicate with each other. Each node extends the network seamlessly.

discovery.text: Your device automatically connects to the nearest node. As you walk around, you hop between nodes without disconnecting.

twist.text: Mesh adds latency — each hop between nodes takes time. For gaming or video calls, a wired backhaul reduces that.

climax.text: Products like Google Nest, Eero, and TP-Link Deco made mesh affordable. Whole-home Wi-Fi became simple to set up.

punchline.text: Mesh spreads Wi-Fi everywhere. No dead zones, no repeaters.

quiz.question: How do mesh networks eliminate Wi-Fi dead zones?
options: Multiple nodes extend coverage and hand off devices seamlessly
They use a single powerful antenna to cover the entire area
They switch to cellular data in weak spots

details.summary: Mesh networks connect multiple wireless nodes that relay traffic for each other, creating a self-healing network without single points of failure. Consumer mesh systems blanket homes in Wi-Fi coverage, while city-scale mesh networks provide community internet.
details.whyItMatters: Mesh networking solves the coverage and reliability problems of single-router setups. Self-healing mesh topologies are also used in IoT, emergency response, and community broadband projects.
takeaways: Nodes relay traffic for each other across multiple hops
Self-healing topology reroutes around failed nodes automatically
Consumer mesh systems provide whole-home Wi-Fi coverage

faq.question: How is mesh Wi-Fi different from a Wi-Fi extender?
faq.answer: Extenders rebroadcast the signal on the same channel, halving throughput. Mesh systems use dedicated backhaul channels between nodes, maintaining full speed. Mesh nodes share a single network name with seamless roaming.

faq.question: What are the limitations of mesh networks?
faq.answer: Each hop adds latency as data is relayed between nodes. Throughput decreases with more hops between the client and the internet gateway. Wired backhaul between nodes solves this but requires cabling.
